name: nagare-architecture-refactor
globalChecks: cd web && npm run format:check && npm run test:ci

tasks.title: Extract the task-attempt lifecycle
tasks.objective: Create one authoritative module for claiming, running, retrying, cancelling, and completing a task attempt while preserving current external behavior.
tasks.architecture: Move lifecycle policy behind a narrow interface shared by local workers, remote workers, the scheduler, and the API. Keep transport, storage, and command execution as injected mechanisms rather than responsibilities of the lifecycle module.
acceptance: A queued task attempt can be claimed at most once under concurrent local and remote workers.
Local and remote execution apply the same retry and terminal-state rules.
Cancelling a logical task resolves and cancels its current attempt without duplicating terminal metrics or logs.
Invalid lifecycle transitions fail explicitly and leave persisted state unchanged.
Lifecycle behavior is covered at the new module boundary.
nonGoals: Do not split the entire Store abstraction.
Do not redesign the worker transport protocol.
Do not change public API payloads unless required to preserve correctness.

tasks.title: Extract the execution-topology projection
tasks.objective: Create a shared, deterministic projection from DAG definitions and run state to the stages and edges rendered by the DAG and run screens.
tasks.architecture: Make topology derivation a pure frontend module. Pages provide definitions and statuses; the projection owns fan-out grouping, fan-in edges, stage order, stable node identity, and status overlays.
acceptance: Mapped tasks and their fan-in and fan-out relationships produce deterministic stages and edges.
Equivalent DAG and run inputs produce the same topology semantics on both screens.
Updating statuses without changing structure preserves node identity and layout order.
Pure projection tests cover ordinary tasks, static fan-out, dynamic map children, and joins.
nonGoals: Do not redesign the visual language of either page.
Do not add a graph-layout dependency.
Do not change backend API payloads.

tasks.title: Extract authoritative run progression
tasks.objective: Create one authoritative service for promoting runnable tasks and deriving a run's terminal state after task-attempt changes.
tasks.architecture: Separate run-level dependency and terminal-state policy from scheduler ticking and persistence mechanics. Feed it task definitions and attempt snapshots; apply returned transitions through injected storage operations.
acceptance: A task becomes runnable exactly when every required predecessor has succeeded.
Failed, killed, and exhausted predecessor attempts prevent invalid downstream promotion.
Run terminal status is derived consistently after completion, retry exhaustion, and cancellation.
Repeated progression is idempotent and does not duplicate task instances.
Scheduler and retry paths use the same progression policy.
nonGoals: Do not introduce a general workflow engine abstraction.

tasks.title: Extract the run-inspection read model
tasks.objective: Create a cohesive read model for run details so the API and frontend consume consistent task, attempt, dependency, timing, and topology information.
tasks.architecture: Build the read model behind a narrow query interface. Keep storage queries and frontend rendering outside it; expose stable DTOs that can be projected into the shared execution topology.
acceptance: Run detail data distinguishes logical tasks from attempts without losing retry history.
Dependencies, timing, status, and logs metadata are assembled consistently in one query path.
The run page consumes the read model without reconstructing lifecycle semantics.
Existing run endpoints remain compatible or receive explicit compatibility adapters.
Read-model tests cover retries, mapped children, missing optional timing, and cancelled runs.
nonGoals: Do not build a general reporting subsystem.
Do not redesign unrelated dashboard pages.
Do not add a new database.
